branchConclusion.supported: In the paired conditional emulator profiles, the modeled RSMB size reaches the memory compare at 0x4c77f97. The resulting compare flags are saved, popped into R10, written to a .dungeon state cell, reloaded into EBX, and remain unchanged on the executed path through `and ebx, 1`. The zero-size profile tests bit 0 as 1 and falls through to 0x4e9935b; the 0x1000 profile tests bit 0 as 0 and takes 0x4e9938c. This establishes conditional-emulation dataflow only.
notEstablished: The paired profiles do not establish what real Windows firmware returns, what this branch means on a real machine, or whether either successor reaches stable game code.
The generic fake payload does not establish which semantic SMBIOS fields are used.
Registry values and CreateFileW behavior are unknown; no result is propagated past these boundaries as game truth.
The API return RVAs do not identify caller functions or function entries.

transferEvidence.operation: GetSystemFirmwareTable returns the modeled size in RAX.
The paired RAX value is present at the shared dispatcher entry.
pop qword ptr [rsp+0x78] stores the saved stack value into dispatcher state.
pop r11 reads the paired 0/0x1000 value from dispatcher stack state.
mov qword ptr [rsi], r11 writes the value to .dungeon address 0x144be849b.
cmp dword ptr [rsi], r10d reads 0/0x1000 from that address with R10D=0xff.
pop r10 reloads the saved compare flags from the captured stack slot.
mov qword ptr [r12], r10 stores 0x293/0x212 at the shared state cell 0x144be8443.
mov ebx, dword ptr [rbx] reloads the state cell into EBX; focused code hooks show EBX unchanged through 0x4e9934f on both captured paths.
and ebx, 1 tests the compare carry flag copied in bit 0; paired successors are 0x4e9935b and 0x4e9938c.
